submitted.rationale: Index 18 (Mn 0.507) gave the highest photocurrent measured, 1.6e-7 A. This composition sits at YMnO3 stoichiometry. MACE puts YMnO3 on the hull and MEGNet predicts a 1.3 eV HSE gap, so it absorbs strongly at 3.22 eV. The merit drops on both sides: 8e-8 A at Mn 0.41 and 2e-8 A at Mn 0.67. That points to a peak near the 1:1 phase.

rejected.reason: YMn2O5 region (Mn 0.67): 2e-8 A, an order of magnitude lower
Y-rich side (Mn 0.41): 8e-8 A. Adding Y2O3 (5.6 eV gap, doesn't absorb) dilutes the absorber
Mostly Y2O3, which doesn't absorb at 3.22 eV, and the measured trend was already falling in that direction

consultations.verdict: Support: YMnO3 (hexagonal) is on hull per MACE with HSE gap ~1.3 eV, well below 3.22 eV photon energy, so Mn:Y~1:1 should form an absorbing stable phase. Index 18 (Mn 0.507) is closest to stoichiometry; measure as anchor.

Support: YMn2O5 is on the MACE hull and has predicted HSE gap 2.78 eV, which the 3.22 eV illumination can excite. Index 15 (Mn 0.670) sits at its stoichiometry, so it probes a different stable absorber from the 1:1 anchor.

Mixed/weak support: Y2O3 (5.6 eV gap) does not absorb at 3.22 eV, so the Y-rich side can only work through the YMnO3 absorber (1.3 eV). At Mn 0.41 the film should still be mostly YMnO3 with some Y2O3, which might passivate it. The merit has been falling toward the Mn-rich side (1.6e-7 at Mn 0.51 vs 2e-8 at Mn 0.67), so moving slightly Y-rich is the best remaining bet, and the GP UCB also picks index 10.
